excerpt: ResearchGate is a free professional network where scientists share papers, ask questions and follow research. Founded in 2008 and based in Berlin; backers include Bill Gates, Benchmark and Goldman Sachs.
content:
ResearchGate is a professional network for scientists and researchers. Members build a profile around their publications, connect with colleagues, discover research and collaborate; an early version of the site described itself as free of charge and designed to meet researchers' needs. It is free for researchers to join. ResearchGate's own press releases in 2025 described the site as used by more than 25 million researchers to share and discover research, build their networks and advance their careers. Publishers can also pay to place their journals' articles on the platform through a programme called Journal Home; in February 2025, for example, the open access publisher MDPI expanded its Journal Home partnership from 10 to 200 journals.

ResearchGate was founded in 2008 by Ijad Madisch, a virologist, with Sören Hofmayer and Horst Fickenscher. VentureBeat reported that the company started in Boston and moved to Berlin, where it is based, and that Madisch is CEO. Its early funding came from Benchmark and Founders Fund. In June 2013 VentureBeat reported a $35 million round led by Bill Gates and Tenaya Capital, with Dragoneer Investment Group and Thrive Capital joining, when the site had about 2.9 million members in 193 countries. GeekWire reported in 2017 that ResearchGate had raised a further $52.6 million from investors including the Wellcome Trust, Goldman Sachs Investment Partners and Four Rivers Group, with Bill Gates investing again.

For researchers the core service costs nothing. Publishers pay for Journal Home partnerships.

This profile draws on published reporting and ResearchGate's partnership announcements; ResearchGate's own pages blocked our checks. We have not tested the service, and nothing here is paid placement.

use_cases: Building a public profile of your publications as a researcher
Discovering new research in your field
Connecting and collaborating with other researchers
Placing a publisher's journal articles in front of researchers through Journal Home

fit: are a researcher, academic or PhD student who wants a visible publication profile
want to follow new work and connect with others in your field
are a publisher looking to reach researchers
not_fit: need a full-text database with guaranteed licensed access
want a general professional network outside science
